S2 fixtures — DECSTBM shape emitted by Claude Code and Codex CLI
Captured 2026-07-31 on macOS 26.5.1 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64), TERM=xterm-256color,
COLORTERM=truecolor.

Each capture ships in two forms. **`.raw.bin` is authoritative.**
  *.raw.bin  — every byte the TUI wrote to the pty master, concatenated, nothing else.
  *.cast     — asciicast v3 (ndjson). Header line, then [interval_s, code, data].
               code "o" = TUI output, "i" = keystrokes the host injected,
               "r" = pty resize, data "COLSxROWS" (TIOCSWINSZ + SIGWINCH).
               Only "o" events should be fed to a VT under test; "r" events must be
               applied as a resize, in order, or the replay diverges.

  ⚠ The two forms are NOT byte-identical, and an earlier version of this file wrongly
  said they were (found in audit round 6). `extract.py` decoded each pty read chunk
  independently, so multibyte box-drawing glyphs that straddle a chunk boundary were split
  and became U+FFFD replacement characters in the `.cast`. Exactly 9 damaged regions, 23
  U+FFFD characters, in three files:
      claude-2.1.220-boot-exit                        2 regions, +9 bytes
      claude-2.1.220-boot-help-status-resize          5 regions, +24 bytes
      codex-cli-0.145.0-boot-status-help-diff-resize  2 regions, +9 bytes
  The two 0.146.0 captures are clean and match their .raw.bin exactly (delta 0). (A round-6
  note said "12 glyphs"; re-derived in round 7, the count is 9 — do not confuse it with the
  9 CSI splice sites of the separate round-5 redaction bug below, which is a coincidence.) The damage is TEXT-ONLY: the CSI/OSC sequence multisets derived from the two
  encodings are identical in all five captures, so every figure the design doc cites holds
  on either form. It is not repaired because the original chunk boundaries are not
  recoverable unambiguously from the committed files, and guessing them would risk
  corrupting evidence to fix a cosmetic defect. **Derive control-sequence facts from
  `.raw.bin`; use `.cast` for timing and resize events.**

Captures
  claude-2.1.220-boot-help-status-resize      120x40 -> 100x24 -> 140x45. /help, /status.
  claude-2.1.220-boot-exit                    120x40. Boot then /exit (clean alt-screen exit).
  codex-cli-0.145.0-boot-status-help-diff-resize  120x40 -> 100x24 -> 140x45. /status /help /diff.
  codex-cli-0.146.0-boot-status-help-resize   120x40 -> 100x24 -> 140x45. /status /help.
  codex-cli-0.146.0-14row-heavy-history-insert 100x14, no resize. Four slash commands on a short
               terminal: the densest history-insert traffic of the set (94 lines scrolled into
               scrollback, no CSI 3J).

No paid model calls were made; only local slash commands were driven.

Redaction — EQUAL-LENGTH ONLY. These captures are byte-addressed by the design doc
(§5.3 cites ESC[?1049h at byte 67 / 1900, and the 0.145.0 pair at 38963 / 43372), and the
rendered panels are column-aligned, so every substitution here MUST preserve byte count.
Do not use the <HOME>/<USER> placeholders used elsewhere in tests/fixtures — they are a
different length and would shift every offset after them.

  - Email addresses -> equal-length placeholder. The placeholder is sized per site, so it
    differs between captures: "redacted@e.invalid" (18 bytes) in the Claude panels,
    "redacted@examp.invalid" (22 bytes) in the Codex /status panel. Match on
    "redacted@" and not on a fixed domain.
  - SECOND PASS, 2026-08-01 (audit rounds 11-12), all equal-length. These are as much a part
    of this corpus's redaction as the email and username entries, and are listed here because
    REVIEW.md sends every reader to this file for the conventions:
      Account display name    <given name> -> "User"        (4 B)  Claude welcome banner
      Codex plan tier         <plan>       -> "Plan ABC"    (8 B)  /status panel
      Codex credit balance    <credits>    -> "0000 credits" (12 B)
      Claude account tier     <tier>       -> "Plan  ABC "  (10 B)
      Recording session UUID  <run uuid>   -> "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003" (36 B),
                              including its ellipsized 34- and 14-byte renderings
    The same UUID was scrubbed from s5 in the same pass; s4 had already replaced it with <UUID>.
  - THIRD PASS, 2026-08-01 (audit round 13), all equal-length. Four MORE live session ids were
    still present -- two Codex /status "Session:" values and two Claude ids inside OSC 777
    terminal-integration notification bodies, a site no CSI-oriented scan reaches:
      <session id A> -> 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004  (36 B, Claude OSC 777)
      <session id B> -> 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005  (36 B, Claude OSC 777)
      <session id C> -> 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006  (36 B, Codex /status)
      <session id D> -> 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000007  (36 B, Codex /status)
    Plus the account usage state the second pass missed:
      Weekly-limit remaining  <pct left>   -> "00% left"    (8 B)
  - FOURTH PASS, 2026-08-01 (audit round 14), all equal-length. The third pass scrubbed the
    usage TEXT and left two things that still encoded the same fact:
      Usage bar glyphs        7 filled of 20 -> 20 empty  (60 B; the bar tracked the real
                              percentage, so "00% left" sat beside a bar still drawing ~35%)
      Limit reset times       <hh:mm> x3   -> "00:00"     (5 B each; the third pass replaced
                              the reset DATES but not the times beside them)
      Limit reset dates       <date>/<date> -> "1 Jan"   (5 B each)
    None of these was caught by REVIEW.md's documented fast pass -- the display name in
    particular is a different string from the login name, so `grep "$(id -un)"` cannot see it.
    RULE, learned by breaking it: record the LENGTH and the REPLACEMENT here, never the original
    value. These notes ship in the same repo as the captures, so writing the original back into
    them re-commits exactly what the pass removed.
  - Username "<name>" (7 bytes) -> "example" (7 bytes). Affects both real home paths
    (/Users/<name>/.codex/... in the codex /status panel) and the path-encoded scratch
    directory (.../-Users-<name>-Desktop-CODING-marion/...). All three /Users occurrences
    in the 0.145.0 capture sit at 19709 / 27142 / 35155, i.e. before 38963, so a
    length-changing substitution would have broken the cited offsets.

Verified after redaction: file lengths, ESC[?1049h/l offsets, CSI 3J and CSI 2J counts,
DECSET 2026 bracket counts, the probe sets (DA1/XTVERSION/CPR/OSC 10/11) and the DECSTBM
region histogram are all unchanged.
No API keys, tokens, or credential-bearing paths were present.

  ⚠ CORRECTION, 2026-08-01 (audit round 5). The claim above was FALSE when first written,
  for the DECSTBM histogram only. The original redaction ran an email regex over raw bytes
  without anchoring to escape-sequence boundaries, so at 9 sites the match began *inside* a
  CSI sequence and consumed its parameter bytes and terminator:
      Claude: ESC[38;2;153;153;153m<email>  ->  ESC[38;2;153;153;r...  (SGR became DECSTBM)
      Codex:  ESC[22m<email>                ->  ESC[r...              (SGR became DECSTBM)
  A VT replaying the committed bytes therefore executed 3 scroll-region ops per affected
  Codex capture that the harness never emitted, and the "histogram unchanged" line was
  self-refuting: analyze.py cannot read .raw.bin at all (it parses an uncommitted .rec
  format and silently returns zeros), so nothing had actually re-derived it.

  Repaired 2026-08-01, length-preserving, in both .raw.bin and .cast. The eaten SGRs were
  recoverable from context — the Claude line's next value uses an intact
  ESC[38;2;153;153;153m, and Codex wraps every /status value in ESC[22m...ESC[2m — so the
  control sequences are restored EXACTLY; only the email text is a placeholder, shortened
  to keep each splice byte-for-byte the same length. Post-repair, re-derived:
      offsets 67 / 1900 / 5866 / 38963 / 43372 and all five file lengths: unchanged
      CSI 3J, CSI 2J, DECSET 2026 brackets, probe sets:                 unchanged
      DECSTBM inside/total, 0.145.0 resize capture:   was 25/27  ->  22/24 (true value)
      DECSTBM inside/total, 0.146.0 14-row capture:   was 29/29  ->  26/26 (true value)
      DECSTBM inside/total, 0.146.0 resize capture:       16/18 (never corrupted)
      DECSTBM inside/total, claude-boot-exit:         was  1/4   ->   0/3  (1 forged site)
      DECSTBM inside/total, claude-boot-help-status-resize: was 2/3 -> 0/1 (2 forged sites)
  The two Claude figures are recorded for completeness -- no design-doc figure cites them, but
  REVIEW.md S4 makes the DECSTBM histogram a re-derive invariant for all of s2, so a reader
  checking them needs the pre-repair baseline to diff against.
  Design doc §5.3 has been corrected to the true values. The 94-lines-scrolled figure in the
  capture list above IS reproducible — `python3 scrollattr.py
  codex-cli-0.146.0-14row-heavy-history-insert` gives 2 + 92 = 94 top-anchored scroll-up lines.
  What is not reproducible from this repo is what an emulator *retains* of them (alacritty 94
  vs vt100 0, and the 121->2 collapse), since no Rust exists yet — design doc §11 item 10.

Tools (copied from the spike scratch dir, throwaway, not workspace code)
  ptyhost.py   pty.fork host: TIOCSWINSZ, scripted keystrokes/resizes, logs all raw bytes.
  extract.py   .rec -> .raw.bin + .cast
               ⚠ Three caveats, found in audit rounds 7/9/12. (a) It decodes each record
               independently for the .cast, which is what split the 9 glyphs above; .raw.bin
               is built from undecoded bytes and is unaffected. (b) Its cast header hardcodes
               cols=120 rows=40, so it cannot have produced
               codex-cli-0.146.0-14row-heavy-history-insert.cast, whose header correctly reads
               100x14. Trust the committed headers, not the tool: an L2/L4.5 replay sized from
               extract.py's default would diverge on exactly the capture the scrollback
               argument rests on. Parameterize cols/rows before regenerating anything.
               (c) scrollattr.py has the SAME hardcode -- it ends with replay(ev, 40, 120) and
               ignores the cast header too, so its "of N rows" annotation is wrong for the
               14-row capture. The 2 + 92 = 94 total is unaffected, because both regions are
               set by explicit DECSTBM rather than inferred from the terminal height.
  analyze.py   distinct DECSTBM regions + counts, DECSET 2026 brackets, alt-screen, scroll prims
  scrollattr.py  VT state machine that attributes every scroll-up / scroll-down event to the
               (see caveat (c) under extract.py: it shares the same hardcoded 40x120 replay)
               DECSTBM region active at that moment — this is what answers the S2 question.
